title: Roger Goodell extends term until 2030
seoTitle: Roger Goodell Extends NFL Contract Until 2030
subtitle: The NFL commissioner secures four more years of leadership
excerpt: NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell signed a new contract extension keeping him at the helm of the league through the 2030 season, reinforcing stability amidst.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell recently confirmed a new contract extension that keeps him at the helm of the league through the 2030 season, bringing stability to a period of important negotiations.

why the extension is in the spotlight

The announcement came amid discussions about the new collective bargaining agreement and potential changes to the league's structure, such as expanding to an 18-game season.

details of the new extension

The contract, which replaces the previous one set to expire in March 2027, extends Goodell's term until March 31, 2031. The agreement is "highly performance-based," with over 95% of the compensation tied to NFL metrics and Goodell's performance, according to the Compensation Committee's memorandum.

financial and media impact

With revenues of around $23 billion in the last fiscal year, the NFL is on the rise. The extension coincides with the conclusion of 11-year media deals worth more than $110 billion. In January, regulators approved ESPN's acquisition of NFL media assets, increasing the league's presence in the broadcasting market.

global expansion and future events

Goodell has been driving the NFL's international presence. In 2026, the league will hold a record nine games outside the country, across four continents and eight stadiums. The commissioner also led the approval of flag football's inclusion in the 2028 Olympics.

history of contract renewals

This is Goodell's fifth renewal, having previously signed extensions in 2009, 2012, 2017, and 2023. He took office in 2006, succeeding Paul Tagliabue, and remains the league's only living commissioner.

next steps in collective bargaining

The current collective bargaining agreement runs through 2030, but negotiations are expected to resume before that deadline, with the possibility of an 18-game season as a central theme.

With information from NFL.com, The New York Times.
